newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota floods continue to delay fieldwork.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota floods continue to delay fieldwork.

text.p: North Dakota flooding continued to delay fieldwork, damage stored commodities and equipment and stress livestock in the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop report.

Wet field conditions and colder than normal temperatures pushed the average starting date for fieldwork to May 4, two days later than the estimate in last week's report and well behind the five-year average of April 22.
No plantings were reported as of April 20, the same as last year. The five-year average shows five percent of spring wheat, four barley and oats and one percent of durum planted.

Ranchers continued to assess livestock losses from the intense April 4-6 blizzard. Cattle and calf death loss was estimated at 95 percent above normal, with the hardest hit areas in the southern half of the state, which were termed "unprecedented," the report said.
Wet, muddy conditions contributed to pneumonia and scours in calves.

Cattle conditions as of April 20 were rated three percent very poor, 14 poor, 35 fair, 46 good and two excellent. Calves were rated five percent very poor, 15 poor, 34 fair, 44 good and two excellent.
